symptom: A bare `create or modify module role M.R;` (no description clause) reported `Modified module role: M.R` and erased the role's stored Description; `describe` → `exec` was unaffected because describe prints the description, and grants (on the entity, keyed by role name) were untouched.
cause: CreateModuleRoleStmt.Description was a plain string, so 'no clause' and `description ''` were the same value, and execCreateModuleRole's OR MODIFY branch passed it to Backend.AddModuleRole, which overwrites the existing role in place.
fix: Description is a *string, nil when unstated, as CreateUserRoleStmt's properties have been since ako/mxcli#707; OR MODIFY writes the stored description when it is nil, so the write is elided and the run reports Unchanged. `description ''` clears it. Adopting an auto-provisioned role still drops its marker description.
insight: A neighbouring statement already had the right shape: the user-role code even said 'the rest keep their stored values, as a module role's missing description does', which was false — a comment asserting a sibling's behaviour is a claim to test, not evidence. The tell for this class is an optional clause parsed into a value type: grep the AST for optional clauses stored as string/bool without a *T or a ...Set flag, then follow each to an OR MODIFY branch. mx check is 0 errors with the fault (measured, 11.13.0), and describe → exec cannot show it because describe restates the value; only a hand-written minimal statement does.
